chapter: New York, the Lafayette and the Cotton Club
title: The 802 union keeps Lunceford's band out; Peekaboo Davis
summary: Crawford says Local 802 refused them membership to slow the band, a delegate named Peekaboo Davis policed it, and they used Buffalo's local 533.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: The only time I've had an 802 musicians union --
Was when you came to New York?
-- by chance -- no, they wouldn't let us in the union. By no means. They were trying to break the band up. We were going -- we were growing too fast.
Well, who was trying to break it up?

Well, I guess the musicians downtown such as Duke Ellington, Calloway, Chick Webb, all of them. They didn't want that band to interfere with their progress or interfere with them. Oh, yes, that was a fact. They had a colored guy by the name of Peekaboo -- Jimmy Peekaboo Davis. He was a bad guy.
Well, who did he work for?

He was a delegate, came around and peeked at everybody. If he didn't want you up there, he said, get off the stand. They'd get off. He didn't bother us like that because they wouldn't let us in this 802 union. I stayed around there for quite a time.
Well now, how did you all -- how were you all working?
We were working out of New York, different colleges and proms.
Now, didn't you -- I mean when you -- when you worked at the Cotton Club, didn't you have to be in the union then? Or did you have to be in the union?
Oh, yes, so you had a union in Buffalo, so you didn't have to, you didn't have to join 802.
533, I think it was. We were union men.
